segments.text: Regulation Change Sentinel. When the rules behind your grants change overnight, which of your compliance decisions are now wrong?

On October first, 2024, the U.S. Uniform Guidance for federal grants, 2 CFR Part 200, was rewritten. The eCFR marks 188 sections as amended. Our demo grants office holds forty-eight documented compliance assessments that quote that text. Re-reviewing all of them is the safe default, and the expensive one.
This is Zetaris, running live on our own server. The Sentinel's three sources are registered here: a PostgreSQL compliance register, a file store with the official text, and the live eCFR API.

One SQL statement reads all three: forty-eight assessments from Postgres, twelve hundred eighty-nine regulation paragraphs from files, and eight hundred seventy-eight version records straight from the government API.
The live API, queried as a table, confirms which sections were amended on October first, 2024.
Then the federated view decides, inside Zetaris, which assessments still stand: twenty editorial only, three unchanged, and twenty-five that need a human.
Here is the review queue, with the exact facts that changed: the equipment threshold, five thousand to ten thousand dollars. The single audit threshold, seven hundred fifty thousand to one million.
For every flagged assessment, the agent shows the quoted text before and after, the facts removed and added, and links to both official versions. A reviewer can check the explanation in seconds.

We measured it against blind labels from an independent annotator. Re-reviewing every amended section flags all forty-eight. Diffing the text flags forty-five. The Sentinel flags twenty-five, and catches sixteen of the nineteen material changes: precision zero point six four instead of zero point four, F1 zero point seven three. The same rule, rewritten in plain Python without Zetaris, agrees on all forty-eight verdicts. Zetaris is slower here, about two seconds instead of half a second per run, which is fine for a job that runs when a regulation changes.
The agent holds one connection. Zetaris federates the database, the files and the live API, and runs the decision as one SQL view.

So why did we think Zetaris was amazing? The moment it clicked was registering the government's eCFR API as a table. One CREATE LIGHTNING REST TABLE statement, and a live federal API could be joined with our Postgres register and a CSV file in the same query. No pipeline, no loader script. Then came the surprise: functions like levenshtein, regexp extract all and array except work inside that federated SQL. So the entire change-detection rule moved out of our agent and into one Zetaris view. We rewrote it in Python as a control, and the two agreed on all forty-eight verdicts. What it let us do: our agent went from three connections and four client libraries to one endpoint, and every verdict it explains carries the source, the version date and the official link. That is exactly what an auditor asks for.
Everything is open source: the SQL, the data pipeline, the evaluation and this demo. Regulation Change Sentinel, built on Zetaris.
